evidence_note: Unreferenced means nothing in src/, tools/, e2e/ or index.html names it. No row here is evidence that its subject works; a BACKEND-ROUTE-PENDING row is evidence only that the command behind it is still registered.

groups.rationale: A wrapper for a backend command that is still registered in lib.rs. The capability is built and reachable from Rust; what is missing is a control in the interface. Deleting the wrapper would move that capability further out of reach, not nearer, so each row is kept and the gate re-checks that the command is still registered. A row whose command has since been unregistered is dead at BOTH ends and fails.

exports.rationale: Contact QC compares a zone top against a fitted fluid contact; no pane offers the comparison yet.
The confirmation a user gives when a log-scale axis is asked to plot zeros; no plot dialog raises it yet.
Lists the aux datasets a core import carried in as extras; the Data Sets pane lists point data by dataset instead.
Removes a stored realization matrix or T2 distribution; nothing offers deletion of an array log yet, so a persisted Monte Carlo matrix can only be replaced by re-running.
Removes one depth-registered plate; the picture panes condition and re-render plates but never drop one.
Writes one named curve set as delimited text with an explicit null token; the export menu offers LAS and the office formats only.
Reads a generic-store curve on its own stored depths; every current reader goes through the aligned fetch instead.
Returns a log set's resolved parameter record and step history. Nothing displays it, which is why the restore path's null manifest (finding 70) has no reader to be wrong for yet.
Describes one module's parameter fields for a generic editor; the parameter dialogs auto-generate from the module manifest instead.
Reads the project's declared absent-value token; import refuses an undeclared sentinel by asking, so nothing reads the stored answer back yet.
The unmapped aux import; the wizard path that confirms a column mapping first is what the Aux button uses.
Names the unit families the engine can convert between; no dialog offers a unit picker driven by it yet.
Names the delimited export formats the backend can write; the export menu hard-codes its entries.
Applies a saved parameter pack across zones; per-well and per-zone parameter editing is the only route offered.
Maps core depths onto the log frame without moving them. Depth registration applies a shift instead, so the non-destructive preview has no control.
Returns the provenance a saved model was fitted under; the saved-models list shows name, metrics and wells but not the citation record.
Writes the whole pinned-well set at once; the Wells pane toggles pins one at a time.
Changes the project depth unit after creation. Deliberately hard to reach: every stored depth is in that unit, so no menu offers it.
Declares the project's absent-value token; the import refusal asks per file rather than recording a project-wide answer.
Reports a problem the startup ladder recovered from. The boot overlay polls the boot report instead, so this second channel has no reader.

groups.rationale: The app reaches this capability through a named live sibling. The row exists so the pairing is written down rather than rediscovered, and the gate re-checks that the sibling is real and is itself referenced - a supersession claim pointing at another dead export would otherwise read as reassurance.

exports.rationale: The pre-wizard core import, which guessed its column roles. The confirm-the-mapping-first import is what the Core button uses; its backend command is now unreached too, and retiring both ends together is a separate change.
The single-file SCAL import. Files selected together are ONE delivery under the universal set rule, so the multi-file wrapper replaced it; its backend command is now unreached too.
Renders a plot at screen proportions. Every caller wants the paper variant, because a deliverable is drawn at a true print scale.
The screen-proportioned PDF twin of renderPlotToSvg, superseded for the same reason.
The fixed blue-green-yellow-red ramp. The extended form takes the colormap and log state the plot properties dialog exposes, including the log-safe maps.
Straight-line least squares. Crossplot v2 offers a choice of regression model, so the panel's own fit carries the model with it.
Returns the range alone and drops the reason a range was refused. Callers take the decision, which is the repo's rule that a refusal is named rather than returned as nothing.
The multi-well binding twin, superseded for the same reason: its refusal says the represented curves do not share one audited range, and the range-only accessor discards that sentence.
Pre-ticked the wells a batch dialog should run on. The shared RUN ON scope selector took that over, so every batch dialog answers the question one way.

groups.rationale: A finished frontend capability with no control wired to it. Unlike a superseded export there is no other way to reach what it does.

exports.rationale: SB-CUT-019 wraps a cut-off as the number AND the unit it was typed in, because 35 where 0.1 is meant is a 350x error whose symptom is a plausible all-net well. The backend refuses a bare number, but every UI path still passes the plain CutoffDefaults shape, so this adapter - and the CUTOFF_UNITS table it is the only reader of - is the entered-form route nothing takes yet.

groups.rationale: A helper, constant or type whose job is done inline at the call sites. Nothing is unreachable; the duplication is the cost, and each row names where it is paid.

exports.rationale: The CPHOTO prefix every core-photograph trace carries. Three sites in coreTraceDialog.ts spell the literal instead, which is how a trace could one day be named something a module reads as lithology.
The wire shape of a plot binding export. The serializer takes the pieces as separate arguments, so the assembled shape is documented here and built in Rust.
Plain-text rendering of the whole processing history, including the UTC marker a zone-less timestamp needs. The History pane has an Export button that builds its own text.
The accessor beside the predicate. Panes ask isWorkingPane whether they are the one that follows the selection; nothing needs to know which pane that is.
Looks one channel's binding out of a list. Callers hold the binding they are working on rather than searching for it.

The validating constructor for the range-position member of the plot-value union, deliberately unclamped so extrapolation beyond a range survives a template. Only the percentile member is constructed today.
A labelled checkbox helper with no sibling field helpers beside it; roughly sixty sites across the panes build a checkbox input directly.
